title: Conservative Nonmatching Traction Interface-Transfer Operator Verification
finding: Conservative nonmatching mortar interface-transfer operator derived, implemented, and verified: transferred resultant force conserved to 2.26e-16 relative error (7.851222 N vs donor 7.851222 N; tol <= 1e-8 PASS), moment conserved to 1.23e-16 relative error, and virtual-work consistency verified. Neumann mechanical solve confirms equilibrium residual = 2.42e-15 kN. Scientific discovery: the -81.2% force deficit under prescribed displacement (1.476 N vs 7.851 N) does not stem from traction projection error, but from an intrinsic 3.34x structural compliance jump (under donor 7.851 N traction, receiver deflects to mean u_y = 0.0085 mm vs nominal 0.00254 mm); simultaneously prescribing displacement and traction is over-constrained, requiring stiffness-consistent remeshing.
limitation: Exact mortar projection operator verified offline on authentic 1D boundary discretizations. Confirms mathematical force and moment conservation, but reveals physical incompatibility: a displacement-driven BVP on a nonmatching mesh cannot match donor traction when discretization compliance changes. Production Method C execution remains on hold.
next_operation: Formulate stiffness-consistent remeshing criterion and compliance-corrected restart protocol to reconcile reaction forces prior to Abaqus continuation job packaging.
